settings.thinkingModeHint: The model reasons before answering: slower, but better at complex tasks. Temperature is ignored in this mode.

settings.translationCorrectionInfo:
After translation, the text is checked automatically for missing fragments, broken markup, links, numbers, placeholders and glossary violations. The check runs without AI and costs nothing.

• Off — the translation is used as is; detected problems are only shown.
• Only if problems are found — the AI model fixes only the detected spots. If there are no problems, no extra request is made.
• Always — the AI model always proofreads and edits the translation. Slower and more expensive, but useful after DeepL and Google: glossary "=" rules, translation instructions and the correction prompt are applied.

Correction runs on the model assigned to translation on the LLM tab. If it fails, the original translation is kept.
settings.translationCorrectionPromptInfo: Extra instructions for the correction in the "Always" mode, e.g. "make the text conversational" or "keep terminology consistent". They are added to the system prompt and the translation instructions without replacing them.
settings.translationGlossaryInfo:
Translation rules (one entry per line):

• Term = Translation — always translate the word or phrase this way, whatever the target language.

• Term = code: Translation; code: Translation — a separate wording for particular languages (a code like es or pt-BR; es also covers es-AR). A translation without a code applies to the other languages.
Example: workspace = es: espacio de trabajo; de: Arbeitsbereich

• !Term — do not translate the word or phrase (keep as is in the entire text).
Example: !TyCo
(An exclamation mark at the start of the line protects the entire phrase after it).

Untranslated terms (!term) work with any translation method. An AI model applies translation rules (=) right away; with DeepL and Google they are applied only when post-translation correction is enabled.
settings.translationGlossaryMachineHint: DeepL and Google without correction only support untranslated terms (!term). To apply translation rules (=), enable post-translation correction.
